headline: Middle East Flashpoint Clouds the Open as Semiconductor Pain Lingers
body_html:
Markets head into Wednesday's open under the shadow of a rapidly deteriorating geopolitical picture in the Middle East. U.S. and Saudi forces struck Iran-backed positions in Iraq overnight, Iran rejected an Omani proposal to ease Strait of Hormuz tensions, and Washington confirmed it intercepted Iranian ballistic missiles fired toward American personnel in the region. Crude prices have climbed in response, and traders will be watching energy futures closely at the bell.

Tuesday's session offered a mixed but broadly constructive tape. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners 323 to 195 across our 519-name universe, with Consumer and Homebuilder names leading at gains of 2.65% and 2.46%, respectively. Healthcare and Software each posted solid advances. The glaring exception was Semiconductors, which shed 5.61% as a group — the worst sector result of the day — dragged lower by severe post-earnings selling in chip-adjacent names.

The catalyst calendar for Wednesday is thin on scheduled data, meaning geopolitical headlines and any corporate guidance updates will likely set the intraday tone. Watch the energy complex for volatility tied to Hormuz developments, and monitor whether Tuesday's semiconductor damage deepens or stabilizes at the open.

briefs.headline: Strait of Hormuz Risk Premium Rises as Iran Rejects Diplomatic Off-Ramp
briefs.body: Tehran's rejection of an Omani-brokered proposal to manage Strait of Hormuz passage removes a key de-escalation path and raises the prospect of sustained supply disruption. Oil markets responded with gains as traders priced in tighter risk premium. A top U.S. oil industry group separately pushed back against any Gulf-backed voluntary toll scheme for the waterway.

briefs.headline: Semiconductors Absorb Sharpest Sector Blow of Tuesday's Session
briefs.body: The semiconductor group tumbled 5.61% on Tuesday, far outpacing every other sector to the downside. Chip-packaging specialist Amkor Technology was the session's worst performer universe-wide, dropping 24.74%, while memory and equipment names Sandisk and Ichor Holdings fell 14.25% and 13.03%, respectively, as earnings disappointments compounded sector anxiety.

briefs.headline: Repligen and Incyte Power Healthcare to a 2.14% Advance
briefs.body: Life-science tools and biotech names drove Healthcare to one of Tuesday's strongest sector finishes. Repligen surged 10.9% to lead the entire universe, while Incyte added 9.3%. BioLife Solutions contributed an additional 7.35% gain, suggesting investors rotated toward domestically driven, non-cyclical healthcare plays amid overseas uncertainty.

briefs.headline: Sherwin-Williams and Armstrong Propel Consumer and Homebuilder Gains
briefs.body: Sherwin-Williams jumped 8.25% and Armstrong World Industries climbed 8.13%, helping Consumer and Homebuilder sectors to gains of 2.65% and 2.46%, respectively — the two best-performing groups on Tuesday. The moves suggest the market continues to find shelter in housing-linked and renovation-oriented names despite the broader geopolitical overhang.

briefs.headline: Houthi Strike on Saudi Tanker Adds Fresh Red Sea Threat to Oil Calculus
briefs.body: Yemen's Houthi forces claimed responsibility for a missile attack on a Saudi oil tanker in the Red Sea, adding another pressure point to already strained global shipping routes. The incident compounds fears of simultaneous disruption in both the Red Sea corridor and the Strait of Hormuz, a combination that could further elevate crude prices heading into Wednesday's session.

briefs.headline: Dow Holds Ground as Blue-Chip Rotation Offsets AI-Trade Wobble
briefs.body: The Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced Tuesday even as momentum in the artificial-intelligence trade showed signs of fatigue, with heavyweights in the chip complex under significant pressure. Broader breadth across Consumer, Healthcare, and Software names cushioned the overall market, while at least one universe name emerged as an active acquirer in the mergers-and-acquisitions arena.
